transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I feel like I’ve lost all interest in teaching and the activities I used to enjoy, and I can’t seem to care about anything the way I used to. Everything just feels completely flat, and I don't know how to get that spark back.
Have you felt this way for most of the last two years, or did this low mood start more recently as a distinct change from how you usually feel?

It wasn't a sudden change, but more of a heavy, joyless feeling that has been building and pretty constant for about a year and a half now. It really started taking hold not long after I took on the extra STEM track and club responsibilities at school. It has just been gradually wearing me down over all this time.
Have you experienced any specific periods over the last year and a half where your mood and energy dropped significantly lower than your current 'baseline' level of feeling joyless?

No, there haven't really been any distinct periods where my mood or energy dropped suddenly lower than this. It has just been a very steady, constant weight that's been building over the entire year and a half. I pretty much feel this same low, joyless energy every single day.
Over this past year and a half, have you also experienced other physical changes, such as trouble sleeping, changes in your appetite, or feeling physically tired or sluggish most days?

Yes, all of those have been a real struggle for me. I lie awake for hours with my mind racing and then wake up at 4 or 5 a.m. unable to get back to sleep, and my appetite has dropped so much that I'm mostly surviving on coffee and my clothes are fitting looser. On top of that, I feel completely drained all the time, to the point where even basic chores like folding laundry feel like climbing a mountain.

Looking back at the time before this year and a half began, would you say you generally felt like yourself and had a higher baseline of mood, or has this low, joyless feeling been present for as long as you can remember?

Before taking on those extra school responsibilities about 18 months ago, I definitely felt like myself and had a much higher baseline of mood. I used to be highly organized, active in a softball league, and loved going on hikes with my husband. This heavy, joyless feeling isn't how I've felt my whole life; it has just been a constant weight over this past year and a half.

During these past 18 months, have you consistently experienced at least five of the following symptoms: feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt, difficulty concentrating, or recurrent thoughts of death, in addition to the changes in sleep, appetite, and energy you mentioned?

Yes, I have. I constantly feel like a failure as a teacher and a wife, and my brain is so foggy that I struggle to focus or make simple decisions. I've also found myself wishing I just wouldn't wake up in the morning, because not being here anymore feels like it would be such a relief.

In addition to the symptoms we discussed, have you experienced any noticeable slowing down of your physical movements or speech, or conversely, have you felt so restless that you were unable to sit still?
I haven't really noticed any significant changes in my physical speed or how I move. I also haven't experienced any extreme restlessness that makes it hard to sit still.

Have you noticed if your ability to think, concentrate, or make simple decisions has become so impaired that others have commented on it, or does it feel like a profound, pervasive slowing of your mental processes?

Yes, my brain feels incredibly foggy, and I constantly get stuck on simple decisions like which teaching unit to start next, whereas I used to be highly organized. I find myself rereading emails multiple times and zoning out during grading, which has caused me to miss deadlines. It's gotten to the point where my principal had to check in on me because of my slipping performance.

opening_question.question: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets the criteria for a moderate depressive episode. She exhibits significant symptoms including loss of interest (anhedonia), sleep disturbance, appetite loss, fatigue, feelings of worthlessness/guilt, and diminished concentration. The symptoms have caused functional impairment in her professional life, but she does not meet the severity threshold for 'severe' depression (F32.2) as she lacks psychomotor retardation/agitation and the symptoms are not described as having psychotic features or complete incapacitation.
